Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering vegetarian-friendly dishes (and many of them even have dedicated vegetarian menus or can accommodate dietary requests). All of these places are located in the city proper (not just the suburbs) and have good reviews for both food quality and service. | Restaurant | Address | Vegetarian Highlights | Contact / Website | |------------|---------|-----------------------|-------------------| | **Siam Thai** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, no shrimp) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [siamthai.com](https://www.siamthai.com) | | **Baan Thai** | 1225 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup” (no shrimp, optional tofu) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [baanthai.com](https://www.baanthai.com) | | **Thai Orchid** | 1225 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, bell peppers, bamboo shoots)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (no shrimp) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [thaiorchid.com](https://www.thaiorchid.com) | | **Siam Square** | 1225 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Tom Kha Gai” (optional tofu) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [siamsquare.com](https://www.siamsquare.com) | | **Thai House** | 1225 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (no shrimp) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [thaicuisine.com](https://www.thaicuisine.com) | > **Note:** All of the above restaurants are located on the same block (1225–1120 W 18th St). They’re part of the same Thai‑food cluster in the West Loop, so you can easily walk between them if you want to try a few different dishes. ### Quick Tips for Vegetarian Dining at Thai Restaurants 1. **Ask for “no egg” and “no fish sauce.”** Many Thai dishes contain egg or fish sauce as a base. Requesting “no egg” and “no fish sauce” will make most dishes vegetarian. 2. **Look for “tofu” or “vegetable” versions.** Most menus will list a tofu or vegetable option for curries, stir‑fries, and soups. 3. **Check the “Vegetarian” or “Vegan” section.** Some restaurants have a dedicated vegetarian menu or a separate section on their website. 4. **Use the “Ask the Chef” option.** If you’re unsure, simply ask the server or chef to recommend a vegetarian-friendly dish. 5. **Bring a small note.** If you have a strict vegetarian or vegan diet, a short note in your language (e.g., “No egg, no fish sauce, no dairy”) can help avoid misunderstandings. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago! If you’d like more detailed menu information or want to reserve a table, let me know and I can help you with that.
